cards.explanation: The answer is terrified. The text says Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous, and then adds, “Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.” (Numbers 22:3) Terrified and dreaded, back to back. That's a whole nation checking the locks.

The answer is Pethor by the Euphrates. The text says Balak sent messengers to summon Balaam at Pethor, “…which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.” (Numbers 22:5) A king sends a whole delegation to bring one man back. That's a summons you can't leave on read.

The answer is to put a curse on them. Balak, king of Moab, says, “So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me.” (Numbers 22:6) He's not asking Balaam to swing a sword. He's asking for words, and he's sure they'll count.

The answer is False. Balak says the people are “…too mighty for me.” and then only says, “Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land…” (Numbers 22:6) He's not bragging about his army, friends. He's asking Balaam for backup, and he knows it.

The answer is True. Balaam says, “Spend the night here, and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” (Numbers 22:8) Notice he doesn't answer on the spot. He tells the men to wait for the LORD's answer, and the princes stay with him.

The answer is blessed. God tells Balaam, “Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed.” (Numbers 22:12) Balak asked for a curse. God's answer comes with a reason, and the reason is that this people are blessed.

The answer is True. Balaam gets up the next morning and tells Balak's princes, “Go back to your homeland, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you.” (Numbers 22:13) He puts it on the LORD, plainly. No hedging, no “let me think about it.”

The answer is to honor him richly. This is Balak's message, carried by the new princes: “…for I will honor you richly and do whatever you say.” (Numbers 22:17) Balak is the one making the promise. He's gone from asking to promising, and I bet Balaam's ears perked up.

The answer is command. Balaam says, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.” (Numbers 22:18) That's a mighty strong answer to a house full of silver and gold. Keep that line in your pocket, friends, because we'll see how it holds up.

The answer is to go with them but do only what God says. God tells Balaam, “Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you.” (Numbers 22:20) Go, with one condition attached. Hold on to that “but,” because God put it right there in the sentence.

The answer is True. The text says, “Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along…” (Numbers 22:22) Balaam is on the road with the princes of Moab, and God's anger is on him. We're about to see what the road has waiting.

The answer is that she turns off into a field. The text says, “When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field.” (Numbers 22:23) She sees what Balaam doesn't. And she changes course right away.

The answer is foot. The text says the donkey “…pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against it.” (Numbers 22:25) She's squeezed in a narrow passage between two vineyards. Balaam's foot ends up in the middle of it.

The answer is that she lies down under Balaam. The text says the donkey “…lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.” (Numbers 22:27) That's a rider whose ride just parked itself. Balaam is furious, and the donkey is the one who has seen the angel.

The answer is that the LORD opens the donkey's mouth. The text says, “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth…” (Numbers 22:28) It's the LORD who does it. Then she asks Balaam what she has done to him that he has beaten her these three times.

The answer is “You have made a fool of me!” After the donkey asks what she has done to him, Balaam answers her this way. (Numbers 22:29) Look at that. A donkey just started talking and he's already arguing back. I think he's too worked up to be surprised.

The answer is False. The donkey asks, “Have I ever treated you this way before?” and Balaam replies, “No.” (Numbers 22:30) She's been his donkey all his life until today. Even Balaam can't argue with her record.

The answer is facedown. The text says, “Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.” (Numbers 22:31) First the donkey's mouth gets opened, and now Balaam's eyes. Once he sees the angel, he goes low.

The answer is that he would have killed Balaam. The angel says, “If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.” (Numbers 22:33) The donkey Balaam kept beating was the one who turned away. Turns out she was doing him a favor the whole time.

The answer is sinned. Balaam bows low and falls facedown (Numbers 22:31). The angel of the LORD asks why he has beaten his donkey, and then Balaam answers, “I have sinned…” (Numbers 22:34) He goes on, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me.” Earlier he told the donkey he'd kill her if he had a sword (Numbers 22:29), and now he's owning up.

The answer is False. Balaam offers to go back home, but the angel of the LORD says, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” (Numbers 22:35) So Balaam goes on with the princes of Balak. Same road, with a clear rule about his words.
